mechanism: Novel GR agonists (dissociated/selective GR agonists: mapracorat, GW870086)
note: Non-steroidal or dissociated GR agonists built on transrepression-over-transactivation cell assays and rodent contact-dermatitis and skin-atrophy models promised steroid efficacy without atrophy or HPA suppression; both clinical candidates stopped after Phase 2.
label: Atopic eczema (SEGRA)

engagement.note: Cell assays separating transrepression from transactivation defined the class; no patient GR-engagement readout was ever published.
engagement.short: Dissociation shown in cells, never in patients
engagement.quote: Here we describe a nonsteroidal selective GR-agonist, ZK 216348, which shows a significant dissociation between transrepression and transactivation both in vitro and in vivo.
engagement.judgement: The GW870086 AD trial (NCT01299610) took 4 mm lesion biopsies for skin thickness and AD markers, but the registry record says the results were not analysed; no skin gene-expression or receptor-occupancy comparison exists for mapracorat either.

dose.model: Rodent contact dermatitis dose-response vs mometasone
dose.note: Rodent models rated ZK 245186 equipotent with mometasone furoate topically; trials ran empirical 0.01-0.1% ranges with no exposure target to test.
dose.short: Rodent equipotency to mometasone never tested
dose.quote: In vivo, using irritant contact dermatitis and T cell-mediated contact allergy models in mice and rats, ZK 245186 showed anti-inflammatory efficacy after topical application similar to the classical glucocorticoids, mometasone furoate and methylprednisolone aceponate.
dose.reason: No exposure target carried into trials
dose.judgement: Opened at 2009 rather than 2004 because Schäcke 2009 is the first paper to state the clinical candidate's topical relative potency against the clinical comparators; the 2004 ZK 216348 work compared against prednisolone. No AD trial compared mapracorat or GW870086 head-to-head with mometasone at the rodent-equipotent dose; the only head-to-head (GW870086 2% vs fluticasone 0.05%) is scored under efficacy.

efficacy.note: ZK 216348 matched prednisolone in mouse skin inflammation; the SEGRA class promise was steroid-level efficacy with fewer side effects.
efficacy.short: SEGRA matches prednisolone in mouse skin
efficacy.quote: In a murine model of skin inflammation, ZK 216348 showed antiinflammatory activity comparable to prednisolone for both systemic and topical application.

efficacy.note: Mouse ICD rated GW870086 equal to fluticasone; in 25 AD patients 2% cream was not superior to placebo while fluticasone 0.05% was.
efficacy.short: GW870086 fails vs placebo; fluticasone works
efficacy.quote: The clinical efficacy of the new selective corticosteroid was not superior to placebo, although a dose-dependent improvement upon treatment was noticed without the onset of skin thinning.
efficacy.reason: Mouse said FP-equal; patients said placebo-equal
efficacy.judgement: Model prediction: Uings 2013 (doi:10.1111/bph.12232), 'In murine models of irritant-induced contact dermatitis and ovalbumin-induced allergic inflammation, GW870086 showed comparable anti-inflammatory efficacy to FP.' Patient result (NCT01299610, results posted 2017-10-16): TIS change vs placebo at day 22 was -0.89 (95% CI -2.00 to 0.23, p=0.118) for GW870086 2% and -0.38 (p=0.48) for 0.2%, versus -1.51 (p=0.011) for fluticasone 0.05% in the same patients, at 40x fluticasone's concentration. Called contra because the model's prediction (FP-comparable) failed on the trial's own criterion; magnitude is recorded as within_2x (59% of the FP effect) so a within-2x rule would re-score this as a match, and n=25 is underpowered. The same year, the other class member matched: Bayer's registry synopsis for mapracorat (EudraCT 2010-024279-14 = NCT01359787, 197 patients, EU register results first published 2015-06-03, https://www.clinicaltrialsregister.eu/ctr-search/trial/2010-024279-14/results) reports 'Statistically significant improvement in EASI from baseline to Visit 6 (EOSM) was observed for the 0.1% and 0.03% mapracorat groups compared with the vehicle' - direction only, no effect sizes given, never peer-reviewed ('Publication(s): None'), and no comparison against mometasone as the rodent model predicted. Contra overrides that match under the rules. Dölle 2015 is paywalled (Karger); status rests on the abstract plus the registry numbers, and I could not confirm whether its discussion references the mouse data (comparison_stated therefore false).

safety.model: Rat skin atrophy and ACTH suppression
safety.note: Rat models predicted partial atrophy sparing but no HPA sparing for ZK 216348; ZK 245186 later showed less atrophy after long-term topical dosing.
safety.short: Rats: less atrophy, same ACTH suppression
safety.quote: A markedly superior side-effect profile was found with regard to increases in blood glucose, spleen involution, and, to a lesser extent, skin atrophy; however, adrenocorticotropic hormone suppression was similar for both compounds.
safety.judgement: The follow-on mapracorat paper (Schäcke 2009, doi:10.1111/j.1476-5381.2009.00238.x) claims 'a better safety profile with regard to growth inhibition and induction of skin atrophy after long-term topical application'. The HPA prediction (no sparing) was never tested in print: Bayer's two mapracorat HPA-axis studies in AD (NCT01408511, NCT01407510, 2011) have no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov or the EU register and no publication.

safety.note: GW870086 0.2-2% caused no ultrasound skin thinning over 42 days in 20 volunteers while clobetasol did, as the dissociation model predicted.
safety.quote: Significant skin thinning was observed in the second study on days 14 and 21 when patients were treated with the comparator but not with the novel corticosteroid compared to placebo.
safety.reason: No atrophy, but no efficacy either
safety.judgement: Mechanically 'same': the published comparison (NCT01381445, 20 healthy volunteers, clobetasol propionate 0.05% comparator, ultrasound skin thickness) agreed with the model's no-atrophy prediction, and the mapracorat 4-week AD trial synopsis adds 'no new safety findings' at the AE level. Scientifically weak: the same compound had no significant efficacy in AD, so absent thinning may reflect too little GR activity in skin rather than true dissociation; the comparator is a superpotent steroid; and no comparison measured HPA suppression, which the 2004 rat model predicted would NOT be spared. NCT01381445 has no results posted on ClinicalTrials.gov and I found no EU-register record for it, so registry_date is null.
